newsitem.title: USA: Explorer pipeline shipments delayed by maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Explorer pipeline shipments delayed by maintenance.

text.p: The Explorer Pipeline system should be back on a normal schedule by the end of May after liftings on jet fuel, gasoline and distillates were pushed back this week, pipeline officials said on Wednesday.

The Houston-to-Chicago Explorer Pipeline system is operating about five days behind schedule following maintenance and a heavy slate of distillate liftings, Bill Fulton, manager of shipping relations, said.
"Hopefully, by the end of May we will be back on schedule," he said. "We will be picking up the rate here in the next few days."
Sources said the Williams pipeline system was accepting additional volumes into the Midwest markets, where traders said spot prices and basis were little affected by the Explorer delays.

The second largest U.S. refined products pipeline, the Explorer system's southern segment from Tulsa to Houston can pump as much as 700,000 barrels per day (bpd) of distillates and gasoline. The pipeline's northern segment from Tulsa to Chicago can move nearly 500,000 bpd of total products volume.
